audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[1] labels Justice Punch as his Q. Justice Punch is Galio's E; Winds of War is the Q.
audit.why: Riot's kit: Colossal Smash (P), Winds of War (Q, 11s at 825 — two windblasts converging into a tornado), Shield of Durand (W, 18s taunt), Justice Punch (E, 11s at 650, knocks up the first champion), Hero's Entrance (R, 180s). Calling the knockup a Q sends you dodging the wrong ability.
audit.corrected: Justice Punch named as the E knockup and Shield of Durand as the W taunt.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page says that both of Galio's CC abilities end an Aegis Assault channel.
audit.why: Riot's Shield of Durand text: on release 'Galio will taunt and damage nearby enemies'. Riot's Justice Punch text: it charges, 'knocking up the first enemy champion he encounters'. Aegis Assault is a channel the kit flags as interruptible by any CC — so a taunt or a knockup does not merely damage you through it, it ends it and wastes 22 seconds. _missing-interactions.json flags both.
audit.corrected: Never start Aegis Assault with Shield of Durand's 18s or Justice Punch's 11s available — either one cancels it outright.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere, and Hero's Entrance is described only as 'his global R'.
audit.why: Justice Punch 11/10/9/8/7, Shield of Durand 18/17/16/15/14, Winds of War 11/10/9/8/7, Hero's Entrance 180/160/140 at 4000/4750/5500 range. Hero's Entrance also shields every ally in the landing zone before it knocks up — a detail that changes whether you contest the lane he lands in. And its 180s matches your Grand Starfall exactly, which is the roam-trading rule the page needed.
audit.corrected: Real numbers throughout; the 180s-against-180s roam trade stated in the level-6 spike.

audit.why: FAV at 54.24% over 1202 games — the strongest win rate in this slice. The chart's shape is right: Pantheon owns levels 2-3 before any MR is stacked, level 6 is the flip because Hero's Entrance answers his own roams, and the item stages come back to Pantheon only if the early lead was banked.

edits.after: Shield Vault's leap-stun plus an empowered Q out-trades a Galio with no MR stacked and Winds of War still on 11s.

edits.after: Full kit online — W-stun into empowered-Q, facing him so Aegis Assault eats Winds of War, is your best pre-6 window.

edits.after: Justice Punch into Shield of Durand's taunt chains CC through your channel, and Hero's Entrance answers your roam on the same 180s as yours.

edits.before: Galio is one of the better early-game tanks but you are flatly stronger levels 1-3 — he has no MR stacks yet, his Q is a slow delayed circle you can step out of, and your point-and-click W-stun lands damage he can't dodge. Lead with the W-stun into an empowered Q for the burst, and use E's directional block to eat his Q poke and passive-empowered autos while you close. Don't trade into his taunt window if he flashes it, but pre-6 his only CC is that telegraphed Q — punish every time it's down.
edits.after: Galio is a strong early tank but you are flatly stronger levels 1-3 — no MR stacked, Winds of War is two windblasts converging into a tornado you can walk out of, and Shield Vault's leap-stun cannot be dodged. Lead W-stun into empowered Q, and face him so Aegis Assault eats the tornado and the Colossal Smash auto. His CC is Justice Punch on 11s and Shield of Durand's taunt on 18s — both end your channel, so punish him every time they are down. Every chunk lands before he has a single magic resist item to soak it.

edits.before: You still control 4-5 with empowered-Q poke and E blocks, but the lane tilts at 6: his ult Hero's Entrance plus Justice Punch taunt turns your all-in into a CC chain that he survives, and his global R means he answers the roams you'd normally cash your lead in for. Keep forcing short W-Q trades and back off the moment his taunt is up — you cannot win an extended fight once he's MR-stacked. Convert tempo into tower plates and objectives, not a coinflip dive.
edits.after: You still control 4-5 with empowered-Q poke, but the lane tilts at 6. Hero's Entrance shields every ally where it lands before knocking up, and it is on 180s — the same as Grand Starfall, so your roam and his answer trade one for one. Never channel Aegis Assault while Justice Punch's 11s or Shield of Durand's 18s taunt are up; both cancel it and you lose 22 seconds for nothing. Convert your tempo into tower plates and objectives instead of a coinflip dive.

edits.before: You out-stat him at level 1 with point-and-click W-stun damage while his Q is slow and he has zero MR stacks yet.
edits.after: You out-stat him at level 1 with Shield Vault's leap-stun while Winds of War is slow and he has no MR stacked yet.

edits.before: Justice Punch into Hero's Entrance taunt turns your all-in into a CC chain he survives, and his global R out-roams you.
edits.after: Justice Punch into Shield of Durand's taunt cuts your channel and chains CC, and Hero's Entrance answers the roam you make.

edits.after: - Galio Justice Punch: 11s at rank 1 — the knockup cancels your Aegis Assault, so never channel into it. - Shield of Durand: 18s taunt, same problem. - Hero's Entrance: 180s. - Shield Vault: 13s, never on chip.

notes: Mirror reused: audits/top/galio__pantheon.json. Same facts from Pantheon's side — Aegis Assault blocks damage from the FRONT only (not untargetable), it is the 22s ability doing the blocking rather than Mortal Will, and Mortal Will merely empowers the next spell. No contradiction: his page says Justice Punch and the Durand taunt beat the channel, mine says the same. I also honoured the mirror's refusal on one point: _missing-interactions.json claims Justice Punch denies Shield Vault and Grand Starfall via a 'terrain' flag, but Riot's description is a step back and a charge that knocks up — it creates no terrain and grounds nothing, so neither page makes a dash-denial claim. The real interaction, the knockup ending the channel, is written on both.
